title: Reading bitwise results
description: You can compare complementary bit patterns and their shifted values.
source: draft: codex free model + edit: codex

steps.description: print_bin scans bit positions from 31 down to zero. You can read its mask-and-shift expression as selecting one position per print.
a is hexadecimal aa, printed as decimal 170, and b is printed as decimal 85. The recording shows complementary low-byte patterns.

steps.question: Which low-byte results does the recording show for AND, OR and XOR?
steps.answer: AND produces all zeros. OR and XOR both produce eight ones in the low byte for these complementary inputs.

steps.description: You see the three results followed by the inverted pattern for a. The recorded inversion also sets the previously zero upper bits.
The two shifts start from c equal to 2. You see 4 after the left shift and 1 after the right shift, each with its printed binary pattern.
